Edge stability plot

Source: R/network-plots.R
plot_edge_stability.Rd

Plots the stability-selection frequency of the most stable edges (up to 50) at the selected penalty, coloured by whether the edge joins two omic layers. The network object stores frequencies at the selected penalty only, so this is not a stability surface over the tuning grid; keep the grid from the estimator if one is needed. A reference line is drawn only when threshold is given.

Usage

plot_edge_stability(network, threshold = NULL)

Arguments

network

CelltypeNetworkResult with stability=TRUE.

threshold

A single number between 0 and 1, or NULL (default). If given, a dashed reference line is drawn at this selection frequency, for example the cut-off used to call stable edges.

Value

A ggplot object.

Examples

features <- c("G1", "G2", "M1")
stability <- matrix(0, 3, 3, dimnames = list(features, features))
stability[1, 3] <- stability[3, 1] <- 0.85
precision <- diag(3)
dimnames(precision) <- list(features, features)
network <- CelltypeNetworkResult(
    precision = precision,
    adjacency = (stability > 0) * 1L,
    stability = stability,
    node_info = S4Vectors::DataFrame(
        feature = features,
        omic_layer = c("transcript", "transcript", "metabolite")
    ),
    celltype = "Monocyte",
    metadata = list(n_donors = 20L)
)
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
    stability_plot <- plot_edge_stability(network, threshold = 0.8)
    inherits(stability_plot, "ggplot")
}
#> [1] TRUE
